title: batch-backstop-heuristic-and-quant-profile-discovery-cli
author: Lena Brooks
description:
Motivation: Some tenants with spiky traffic hit pathological batch formation where the serving runtime waits to reach a preferred batch shape, causing latency SLO misses and increased tail cost. This PR introduces a conservative "batch backstop" heuristic that detects low-probability/low-reward batching situations and routes those requests through a prioritized single-request fast-path while preserving batching economics for steady workloads.

What this PR does: introduces a lightweight backstop scheduler in the runtime, adds a CLI-driven quantization-profile discovery tool that runs fast micro-sweeps on sampled tenant traces to suggest candidate quant profiles, and wires telemetry & rule metadata so the Optimize service can consume recommended defaults. The work is intentionally modular: the backstop scheduler is a small routing layer inside the batcher; the quant discovery CLI is an opt-in tool that writes candidate profiles as policy snippets (presets) and supports dry-run scoring against historical captures.

High-level changes: runtime/backstop scheduler that evaluates batch-formation probability and expected unit-econ delta; fast-path routing preserving priority and KV cache reusability when safe; quant-discovery CLI (redwood cli quant-discover) that performs lightweight inference checks across model variants (fp16 / int8 / q4_0) and reports estimated latency/cost/quality delta; telemetry markers and lightweight evaluation hooks for offline scoring; docs and operator playbook for reviewing suggested profiles.

Why distinct from prior work: unlike bulk autotuners, quant discovery here is tenant-scoped, fast (minutes), and conservative by default — it only suggests profiles where quality deltas are within configured thresholds and where unit-econ wins exceed a safety margin. The backstop is deliberately simple (probability threshold + expected-cost delta) to avoid oscillation, and includes a short-lived soft-fail counter to prevent flapping during bursts.

How to test: CLI supports --dry-run with a sample capture and prints a ranked CSV. Unit tests include deterministic micro-schedulers and a mock trace harness. Integration smoke tests run the CLI against a small local model and assert telemetry emission and policy artifact creation.

Risk and rollout: feature guarded behind a runtime flag (enable_batch_backstop) and CLI is opt-in. Default behavior remains unchanged. First rollout is to internal staging tenants for two weeks with telemetry gating and automatic rollback if tail-P99 latency regresses >5% or token cost reduction <1%.

Related: ENG-3110 (tenant-level quant onboarding), ENG-2912 (batcher stability incident follow-up).

Final state: 3 approvals, no outstanding change requests.
release_notes: Add: runtime batch backstop heuristic (guarded) to reduce tail latency for sparse/spiky workloads. Add: redwood cli quant-discover to generate conservative tenant-scoped quant profile suggestions. Operators: follow docs/ops/batch-backstop-playbook.md for rollout and gating.
notes_for_ops: Default flag is off. Staging rollout plan included in playbook. Watch P99 latency, unit-econ CSV, and quant discovery recommendation adoption rate. If post-rollout telemetry shows >5% P99 regression, automatic rollback will disable backstop and delete newly-applied candidate profiles.
